77395.subject:
[Action Required] Update your Gemini API billing in Google AI Studio
 by Oct 12, 2026
77395.body:
Google AI Studio is transitioning from Postpay to Prepay billing for Gemini  
API usage.







Hello Oleg,

We are writing to inform you of an upcoming billing change to Google AI  
Studio and the Gemini API.

We require developers to switch your Gemini API billing from Postpay to  
Prepay by October 12, 2026. This is part of our ongoing effort to improve  
our platform to give developers more control over API consumption and costs.

This change applies exclusively to your Gemini API usage in AI Studio. All  
other GCP services on your account will remain on Postpay.

What you need to know

Key changes:
Starting October 12, 2026, to use paid features in the Gemini API you will  
be required to change the billing plan associated with your Google AI  
Studio projects to Prepay. Learn more about the Prepay billing plan here.

Potential impact:
If you do not transition to Prepay and purchase credits before October 12,  
2026, your service will be interrupted.

What you need to do

Action required:


If you use, or plan to use, paid features in the Gemini API:

Switch to Prepay: Transition to Prepay on the AI Studio billing page and  
purchase credits to continue using paid Gemini API features
Recommendations:

Switch before the October 12, 2026 migration date to avoid service  
interruptions
Configure auto-reload to automatically top up your Prepay balance and  
prevent future service interruptions
View your current billing plan, manage payment methods, and switch to  
Prepay on the AI Studio billing page


No action is required if you do not currently use paid features in the  
Gemini API

We're here to help

If you have any questions or require assistance regarding this transition,  
please review our updated billing documentation.

Thank you for choosing Google AI Studio.





– The Google AI Studio Team




© 2026 Google LLC 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA
This email was sent to novosadovoleg@gmail.com because you signed up to try  
the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

77393.subject: Memecoin Launchpad Fees Grew 77% in a Month
77393.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These were the biggest crypto and DeFi stories today:

* **[Launchpad fees](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-launchpad-fee-share-falls-robinhood-chain-pons-noxa)**[ grew 77% in a month and Robinhood Chain built almost all of it](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-launchpad-fee-share-falls-robinhood-chain-pons-noxa)

* **[Solana Foundation](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/solana-foundation-kingmaking-debate-flash-trade-lily-liu)**[ president Lily Liu rejects “kingmaking” after a perps founder quits](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/solana-foundation-kingmaking-debate-flash-trade-lily-liu)

* **[Franklin Templeton](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/sec-staff-clears-franklin-funds-to-use-onchain-money-fund-for-cash-and-collateral)**[ wins staff relief to use its onchain money fund as registered-fund collateral](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/sec-staff-clears-franklin-funds-to-use-onchain-money-fund-for-cash-and-collateral)

* **[Boltz’s founders](https://thedefiant.io/news/infrastructure/boltz-founders-exit-as-unnamed-bitcoin-group-agrees-to-take-over-suspended-swap-service)**[ walk and hand the suspended swap service to an unnamed Bitcoin group](https://thedefiant.io/news/infrastructure/boltz-founders-exit-as-unnamed-bitcoin-group-agrees-to-take-over-suspended-swap-service)

* **[Harmony](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/harmony-patches-pre-staking-quorum-and-receipt-replay-flaws-after-one-mint-claim)**[ patches two verification flaws after a claim that four billion ONE was minted](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/harmony-patches-pre-staking-quorum-and-receipt-replay-flaws-after-one-mint-claim)

Launchpads collected $75.39 million in fees over the 30 days to Aug. 11, against $42.53 million in the month before that. Nearly all of the $32.86 million of growth came off a chain that opened its public mainnet six weeks ago.

[Robinhood Chain produced $33.49 million of those fees](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pump-fun-launchpad-fee-share-falls-robinhood-chain-pons-noxa), up 236% from the $9.97 million of its own first month, by The Defiant’s calculation from DefiLlama daily fee data across 125 launchpads. Solana did $33.61 million and grew 18%. The four largest new entrants of the period — Pons, StonkBrokers, LetsCash and Uniswap’s Pools — all launched on Robinhood Chain. Pump.fun’s share of the category fell to 42.2% from 57.5% while its own take rose 30% to $31.83 million.

None of it reached prices. The memecoin sector was worth $25.15 billion on Wednesday, 83% below its December 2024 peak, roughly flat over 30 days and down about a third over 90. Across the 5,774 memecoins CoinGecko prices with a market capitalization, the median one sits 99% below its record. What expanded is the toll booth: 1% swap fees at NOXA and Pons, 1.25% on pump.fun’s bonding curve, 125 venues charging on launch churn. Robinhood Chain supplied the churn, $16.58 billion in DEX volume over 30 days agains

Harmony said in Asian morning hours that it is coordinating with exchanges to freeze funds and preparing a software fix. More details 🏛️ Bank of England to test stablecoins and a digital pound in cross-border finance The BOE-led Digital Pound Lab will trial trade-finance interoperability in which exporters receive stablecoins while importers settle in a potential digital pound. It is one of the most concrete signals yet that a major central bank sees privately issued stablecoins and public digital money operating side by side rather than in competition. Read more 💼 Fidelity moves to add staking and quarterly payouts to its ether ETF Fidelity filed to introduce staking to its roughly $900 million ether fund, with rewards distributed to shareholders on a quarterly basis. The structure keeps 85% of gross staking rewards for the fund, with the remaining 15% routed to service providers — a template other issuers are likely to copy.
